subject: Newbie question -- where to declare imported parameter values?

messages.author: bacb0402e67daa77
messages.subject: Newbie question -- where to declare imported parameter values?
parts:
Hi all, new to both stats and Stan.
Say I have a simple model obeying

dCdt[1] <- k1 * C1 / (A + B) - k2 * C2 / (D + E)
dCdt[2] <- k1 * C2 / (A + B) - k2 * C1 / (D + E)

and I am trying to fit dCdt[1] to experimental values of C[1] at T time points. Say the values of k1 and k2 at each of these time points has also been collected and do not need to be fit such that there are T values of k1 and k2. Would I declare these values in the data block such that I have

data {
int<lower=1> T; // Number of time points to fit
real y[T]; // Measured heterotrophic CO2 for each T
real k1[T];
real k2[T];
}

or in the parameter block?
Thanks for your help.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Newbie question -- where to declare imported parameter values?
parts:
If it's a known quantity whose value is given to the program,
it goes in the data block. If it's an unknown you're trying to
estimate, it goes in the parameter block.

But if you're asking that question, you may want to study some
other Stan programs before trying to write your own. Especially if
you're tyring to fit an ODE-based model. (We'll be rolling out
much better solvers soon, but it doesn't look like they'll get into
2.10).

- Bob

parts:
Thanks for your help, Bob. I've gotten some non-ODE toy models working at this point, but am still a bit stuck in terms of ODEs and haven't been able to find too many examples. As I am working with soil carbon models myself, I looked at your soil carbon example, which has been helpful -- I just need some clarification about initial conditions. So here is my functions block right now:

functions {
real[] toyODE(real t,
real[] MGE,
real[] theta,
real[] I,
real[] LIT,
real[] MIC,
real CO2,
real[] x_r,
int[] x_i) {
real A1;
real A2;
A1 <- MIC[1] * LIT[1] / (1 + LIT[1] + LIT[2]);
A2 <- MIC[2] * LIT[2] / (1 + LIT[1] + LIT[2]);
dLITdt[1] <- I[1] - theta[1] * A1;
dLITdt[2] <- I[2] - theta[2] * A2;
dMICdt[1] <- MGE[1] * A1 - theta[3] * A2;
dMICdt[2] <- MGE[2] * A2 - theta[4] * A1;
dCO2dt <- ((1 - MGE[1]) * A1) + ((1 - MGE[2]) * A2)
return dCO2dt

I want to start MIC[2] and LIT[2] at 0.1. For CO2, I would like to start from 0. For my initial conditions y0, I imagine I would have something like y0 = [0.1,0.1,0.1,0.1,0] (using PyStan), and have that as an argument in my integrate_ode line. How would I then assign each initial condition to each variable?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Newbie question -- where to declare imported parameter values?
parts:
The ODE system function has to exactly follow the
signature (arguments and argument types) outlined in
the manual. There is a real array of parameters, a real
array of data, and a real array of int as arguments.

- Bob
